chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Endurance descends according to the measure of the affliction, and whoever strikes his hand on his thigh at the time of his affliction, his reward is invalidated.

key_terms.ضَرْب الْيَد عَلَى الْفَخِذ: Striking the hand on the thigh (a gesture of grief)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of striking the thigh during grief in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) teaches that the level of patience one exhibits is proportional to the severity of the calamity. He specifically notes that the common gesture of grief, striking the thigh with the hand, causes one's good deeds to be nullified. This teaching is often contextualized within Shia jurisprudence as a distinction between natural, involuntary expressions of sorrow and the deliberate, excessive gesture of *darb al-fakhidh* (striking the thigh), which signifies a loss of composure and thus diminishes the spiritual reward of patience.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 144. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Endurance comes according to the affliction. He who beats his hand on the thigh in his affliction ruins all his good actions.
